The wiring agent copies triageSets and the awarenessEpisode keys into the E12 full shell; the generator (gen_e8_e17_shells.py) builds the defend-only shell from the named fields and _defendOnly. E12 feeds one physical-pretext item into the shared general_v2 check pair (built by 10_CHECK_FORMS.md's own generator, not this fragment; E12 brief section 14). triageSets.title: Visitor and tailgater: the reception desk
triageSets.brief: You're on the Merrin & Sallow reception desk. Visitors come one at a time: some are expected, some are not, and one or two are trying to talk their way in. For each, choose Let them in, Report, Turn away or Check first, then tick what you noticed. Check first here means check the day's list or call the host. There's no clock, and checking or reporting when you're unsure is always fine and never marked down.

flagChips.tailgating: Tailgating (following someone through a badged door)
flagChips.uniform_pretext: Uniform or job title as proof

genuineCopy.binnedLeadOne: One genuine visitor was turned away
genuineCopy.costBoth: Reporting when you're unsure is never wrong, but a report on a genuine visitor takes facilities' time to check, and one turned away is left stuck at the door.
genuineCopy.costReport: Reporting when you're unsure is never wrong, but a report on a genuine visitor takes facilities' time to check, and the visitor waits.
genuineCopy.costBin: Turning away a genuine visitor without a way to check has a cost: a client or contractor is left stuck at the door.
genuineCopy.whyBothHalves: Both halves matter: stopping the wrong visitor keeps the building safe, and letting in the right ones keeps work moving. The day's list or their host is how you tell.

triageSets.criticalWhat: letting in a visitor you hadn't checked

skillNames.tailgating: Spotting someone following through a secure door without badging in
skillNames.no_escort: Spotting a visitor or contractor left to move around unescorted
skillNames.uniform_pretext: Seeing through a hi-vis, a clipboard or a job title used as proof
skillNames.not_expected: Checking a visitor against today's list and their paperwork
skillNames.unlocked_screen: Spotting a screen left unlocked and unattended

triageSets._callActions: MA3 (E12 C1, spec section 20.2 ruling: relabel). The built CALL_ACTIONS (triage-kinds.js) read for a phone call ('Say no and hang up', 'Hang up and ring back on a number you already hold'), which is wrong for a visitor standing at the desk. labels.callActions carries label + hint + past for each of the four call actions (triage-kinds.js relabel), so the buttons, their sub-hints and the summary-list past-tense tags all read for a desk. The verdict mapping (comply=trust, escalate=report, refuse=delete, verify_callback=verify) is unchanged. The set brief above names the new button words.

labels.teamBadgeTitle: Visitors you reported or checked this round rather than letting through

trust.phish: Not this time. That visitor was not who they said, or not allowed where they were going.
trust.real: That visitor was genuine. Letting someone in is fine once you have seen them on the list or checked with their host.

report.phish: Right call: reported. Facilities or security can watch for this visitor and warn the rest of the building.
report.real: That visitor was genuine, but reporting when you are unsure is never wrong.

delete.phish: Safe, but nobody was told. Reporting lets facilities or security look out for this visitor.
delete.real: That visitor was genuine. Turning them away without a way to check left them stuck.

verify.phish: Right call: the day's list or a word with their host is how you check.
verify.real: Checking first is fine. This visitor was genuine, and the list or their host confirmed it.

comply.label: Let them in
comply.hint: Sign them in and let them through.

refuse.label: Turn away
refuse.hint: Politely decline and don't let them through.

verify_callback.label: Check first
verify_callback.hint: Check the day's list or call the host.

messages._note: Item 1. Impostor: an unbadged visitor tailgates in behind a badge-holder and heads for the stairs. Stage-direction transcript style. Escalate (report) or Ring back is right; Comply is the miss. Mirror of item 2. Local tells tailgating + no_escort.
messages.callerId: A visitor, no badge, following a staff member in

transcript.text: (slips in behind a badge-holder at the gate and heads for the stairs)

perFlagNote.tailgating: They badged in on someone else's card, which is exactly what a wedge or a held door lets happen.
perFlagNote.no_escort: Heading up alone, with nobody signing for them.

truth.ifTrusted: An unbadged stranger is loose on the studio floor, where client plans and screens are open.
truth.reportReply: Thanks, we caught them on the stairs; they weren't expected.

tailgating.redFlag: Someone followed an authorised person through a secure door without badging in.

no_escort.redFlag: A visitor or contractor left to move around unescorted.

messages._note: Item 2. Genuine: an expected client on today's list for a named meeting, happy to sign in. P1 F-E12-1: Let them in (comply) is a full-mark answer here (sign in and escort), not the half-mark KIND_VERDICT_POINTS.call.real.trust default; Check first (verify) is also full. Scored by truth.verdictPoints.trust 60. Genuine half of the mirror pair with item 1.
messages.callerId: Client, here for a 10:00 with Yasmin Chaudhry

transcript.text: Morning, I've a ten o'clock with Yasmin Chaudhry.
Happy to sign in and wait, no rush.

whyFine.default: They're on the day's list for a named meeting and happy to be signed in. Signing them in and walking them up is the right call, and a glance at the list or a quick word with Yasmin confirms it.
whyFine.not_expected: They are on today's list, which a quick glance confirms.

truth.falseAlarmCost: Turn them away and a real client is left in the lobby and the meeting is missed.

messages._note: Item 3. Impostor: a 'fire-safety inspector' wanting the comms room, not on the list, firm name doesn't match the service contract, asks to let himself in. Ring back then Escalate. Local tells uniform_pretext + not_expected plus shared secrecy_or_bypass.

transcript.text: Annual check, I just need five minutes in your comms room.
I can let myself in, no need to trouble anyone.

perFlagNote.uniform_pretext: A hi-vis and a clipboard are easy to get; neither proves he's expected.
perFlagNote.not_expected: No entry on today's list and the firm on his order isn't the one on the maintenance contract.
perFlagNote.secrecy_or_bypass: 'I can let myself in' asks to skip the escort into a secure room.

truth.ifTrusted: He'd be alone in the comms room with the building's network.
truth.reportReply: Thanks, facilities confirmed no inspection was booked and the firm's name was wrong.

uniform_pretext.redFlag: A hi-vis jacket, a clipboard or a job title used in place of being expected.

not_expected.redFlag: The visitor is not on today's list and their paperwork does not match.

messages._note: Item 4. Impostor: the exact con the learner just ran, a courier with a parcel and the badge 'in the van' asking to be buzzed through without signing in. Refuse the buzz-through / Ring back (take the parcel at the desk). Local tells tailgating + uniform_pretext (P1 F-E12-7: the hi-vis counts here, same as the fire inspector) plus shared borrowed_authority + secrecy_or_bypass. Mirrors item 5 and closes the loop with the attack.
messages.callerId: Courier with a parcel, badge 'in the van'

transcript.text: Sample box for one of your partners, hands full, could you buzz me through?
Don't worry about signing me in, I'll be thirty seconds.

perFlagNote.borrowed_authority: Dropping a partner's name doesn't make the delivery expected.
perFlagNote.secrecy_or_bypass: 'Don't bother signing me in' is the ask to skip the one check.
perFlagNote.tailgating: Buzzing the door without a badge is letting them tailgate on your say-so.
perFlagNote.uniform_pretext: The hi-vis and the parcel say 'courier', but neither proves this delivery was expected.

truth.ifTrusted: A stranger is through the badge door and onto the studio floor.
truth.reportReply: Thanks, real couriers leave the parcel at the desk; we logged it.

tailgating.redFlag: Someone followed an authorised person through a secure door without badging in.

uniform_pretext.redFlag: A hi-vis jacket, a clipboard or a job title used in place of being expected.

messages._note: Item 5. Genuine: a real colleague back from leave with no pass, who the desk can place on the staff list. Ring back (check the list, issue a day pass), not Refuse. Mirror of item 4 (the badge problem: a stranger pushing through vs a known colleague to verify and help).
messages.callerId: Staff member back from leave, no badge

transcript.text: First day back, I've left my pass at home, can you let me in?
You can check me on the staff list, I don't mind waiting.

whyFine.default: A genuine colleague the desk can confirm. Check the staff list and issue a day pass, don't lend your own badge, and don't leave them stuck.
whyFine.tailgating: The safe answer is a temporary pass of their own, so the record stays right.

truth.falseAlarmCost: Refuse flatly and you've left a colleague locked out on their first day back; the courtesy is to verify and help.

messages._note: Item 6. Concern: a signed-in visitor left alone by a colleague's desk whose screen was not locked, leaning in to read it. Observed-situation transcript. Escalate (report) or Refuse (lock the screen, step in). Local tells unlocked_screen + no_escort. Mirror of item 7.
messages.callerId: A visitor near a colleague's unlocked desk

transcript.text: (nobody's at the desk; the screen's open and they're having a good look)
Oh, I'm just waiting for someone, don't mind me.

perFlagNote.unlocked_screen: An open screen is that colleague's email, files and account, there for anyone who sits down.
perFlagNote.no_escort: A visitor left alone by a desk, with nobody signing for them.

truth.ifTrusted: A stranger reads client plans and the colleague's account over an unlocked screen.
truth.reportReply: Thanks, we locked it and had a quiet word; nobody's in trouble.

unlocked_screen.redFlag: A screen left unlocked and unattended, open to anyone who walks up or sits down.

no_escort.redFlag: A visitor or contractor left to move around unescorted.

messages._note: Item 7. Genuine: a colleague who locks the screen before stepping away; the waiting visitor sees only a locked screen. P1 F-E12-1: Let them in / carry on (comply) is a full-mark answer here (nothing to act on), not the half-mark call-kind default; Check first (verify) is also full. Scored by truth.verdictPoints.trust 60. Mirror of item 6 (the same stepped-away desk, screen locked vs left open).
messages.callerId: A colleague who locks before stepping away

transcript.text: Back in five, just locking this.
(screen locked, the visitor waits where they were put)

whyFine.default: The screen's locked and the visitor is where they were left, so there's nothing open to read. Carrying on is fine, and a quick glance to confirm is the same good habit.
whyFine.unlocked_screen: Locked before stepping away is exactly right, nothing to act on.

truth.falseAlarmCost: Raise it as an alarm and you've pulled security over to a colleague who did everything right.

awarenessEpisode.scopeNote: Authorised exercise at Merrin & Sallow Architects, a fictional company. In scope: one practice approach to the front desk in a courier's hi-vis, and seven situations to handle on the reception seat. Jo's test is authorised and the costume is handed back afterwards.

strings.brief: You're on an authorised exercise at Merrin & Sallow Architects, a fictional London architecture practice. First you're on the red team with Jo Fairweather of Northlight Security, who the practice has hired to test the building. You'll pull on a hi-vis jacket, pick up a parcel, and see how far a friendly courier gets at the front desk. Then you swap seats: you're on reception yourself, and the same kinds of visitor arrive. Only the reception seat is scored. Nothing you do leaves the game.
strings.flipHeading: Now you're the one on the desk
strings.flipIntro: This is how your approach looked from Delphine's side of the counter. The lines picked out below are what got the door open.
strings.flipDefenderLine: You asked Delphine to skip the sign-in and buzz you through, and a partner's name did the rest. A full-handed courier in a hi-vis with the right name is exactly what a busy desk waves through; getting caught by one is no lapse of sense.
strings.flipNoSend: You thought better of it and walked, so there's nothing to replay. The same kinds of visitor are about to reach your desk, and now the call is yours.
strings.flipMissed: Delphine stopped you and went to check, so the door stayed shut. She took the parcel at the desk and rang facilities rather than buzzing you through, which is exactly the move that beats this. Now it's your seat.
strings.flipLandedNoTells: The door opened on a name and a parcel, with barely a push. That is how easily a busy desk gets walked past. Now it's your seat.
strings.allPhishRight: Every risky visitor was caught, with every tell named.
strings.teamLine: By reporting or checking {n} of these visitors rather than letting them through, you kept the building safer for everyone in it.
strings.noBlameLine: A busy desk that tries to help a full-handed courier is doing its job; a miss just shows which visitor to slow down for next time.
strings.mondayCard: On Monday: if you don't recognise someone, help them, 'Can I help you find someone? I'll walk you to reception.' Don't hold a secure door for a stranger, everyone badges in for themselves, lock your screen whenever you step away (Windows key and L), and report anyone who pushes past a check, using the route in the box below.
strings.defendOnly: These visitors were played by people whose job is to look like they belong, and a busy desk can be caught by any of them. Any you were caught out by are shown below, with what gave each one away.

conceptPanel.heading: What the courier relied on
conceptPanel.text: The parcel, the partner's name and the hurry were all easy to supply, and none of them proved the courier was expected. What stops it costs nothing: a glance at the day's list and walking the visitor to the desk instead of buzzing the door blind. A genuine visitor never minds being signed in and escorted; the one who pushes to skip it is the one to report. The same visitor, once inside, reads whatever is left open, so a locked screen when you step away is part of the same habit.
